summary: Customer is on a renewal cadence and expects a modest contract extension plus a region add (EU) and reserved capacity bump. Primary blockers are procurement timeline and wanting an on-prem/private pilot for data residency. Team asked for benchmark numbers and written amendment; Redwood AE/SE to provide costs and run an EU pilot test. Security requirements discussed (SOC2, KMS, SSO).
questions: What exact SLO/latency bound do you need for EU?
Will data residency require an air-gapped on-prem package or VPC with private control plane?
What is your preferred contract term length and payment cadence?
transcript:
Header: 2026-08-17 14:00 UTC | Duration: 47m | Attendees: Maya T., Liam C., Arjun P. (Redwood) — Nina P., Carlos R., Leah M., Omar H. (Stratamax)

Summary: quick renewal check-in, scope growth + region add, ask for benchmarks and pricing amendment.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Maya): hey everyone thanks for jumping on, uh this is Maya from Redwood, with Liam our SE and Arjun on CS. how's everyone doing?
00:06 Speaker 2 (Nina): hey Maya, doing good. lots going on, thanks for aligning.
00:10 Speaker 1 (Maya): great. the goal today is just to run through renewal asks, the eu region pilot, and any blockers with procurement so we can get you an amendment.
00:22 Speaker 3 (Leah): we ran the usage numbers, roughly 20% growth q/q, and we expect a spike around black friday, could be higher.
00:31 Speaker 2 (Liam): okay so capacity wise are you thinking a permanent reserved bump or burst/seasonal?
00:36 Speaker 3 (Leah): we prefer reserved for predictability but want a small burst pool for peaks. cost is a factor though.
00:45 Speaker 4 (Carlos): also latency, EU users need <120ms tail p95 for the inference route used in search.
00:53 Speaker 2 (Liam): that helps. for EU we can do hosted eu region or private eu VPC; private pilot gives residency/keys but takes longer to provision.
01:03 Speaker 5 (Omar): procurement here — we need SOC2 type 2 evidence, KMS integration details, and a standard data processing addendum. can you supply those?
01:12 Speaker 1 (Maya): yes we'll attach SOC2 report, KMS integration notes, and a DPA. we also have an on-prem package if needed but need to scope the timeline.
01:24 Speaker 3 (Nina): quick question, for private VPC, will Redwood still manage the control plane or do we host everything? there was some confusion in the doc we saw.
01:33 Speaker 2 (Liam): currently private VPC is customer networking + Redwood control plane; on-prem/airgapped is full customer control. we can make that explicit in the amendment.
01:44 Speaker 3 (Nina): hmm okay. for compliance we might need HSM-backed keys. do you support that with KMS/HSM integrations?
01:51 Speaker 2 (Liam): yes we integrate with cloud KMS and have optional HSM flow — I'll put the integration diagram in the follow-up.
02:00 Speaker 3 (Leah): great. timeline wise procurement is aiming to sign by end of month (Aug 31) if we can get numbers and docs by next week.
02:09 Speaker 1 (Maya): understood. we'll prioritize the amendment. one thing — any competitors you're evaluating?
02:16 Speaker 4 (Carlos): we've looked at CloudModelX for price and VertexServe for private options but Redwood's latency profile is compelling.
02:24 Speaker 2 (Liam): noted. on the EU perf bench — we can run a 10k request job to emulate your traffic. want us to run with kv-cache warmed?
02:34 Speaker 3 (Nina): yes please replicate prod distribution: prefix caching on search, and short sequences (avg 60 tokens).
02:42 Speaker 2 (Liam): okay we'll mirror that. expected output will be p50/p95/p99 and tail latencies plus token cost estimate.
02:51 Speaker 5 (Omar): about the pricing, we prefer quarter billing aligned with our usage window, can you do net-30?
02:58 Speaker 1 (Maya): payment terms we can align with Finance, net-30 is standard for enterprise — we'll propose in the amendment.
03:06 Speaker 3 (Leah): one more technical: if we do a canary model rollout across eu and us, how does Redwood handle fallback if eu capacity is saturated?
03:16 Speaker 2 (Liam): we support smart routing — you can specify region preference and fallback to a compatible variant (slightly quantized model) to keep latency but reduce cost. we'll document the policy.
03:27 Speaker 3 (Nina): perfect. also curious about observability retention, we need 90 days of traces for audits.
03:34 Speaker 1 (Maya): that's an add-on, we have a premium observability retention plan, we'll include pricing options.
03:41 Speaker 4 (Carlos): okay great. can you also outline rollback/metrics that you monitor for quality regressions during rollout?
03:48 Speaker 2 (Liam): yes — we'll include eval hooks (prompt sets), regression alerting thresholds, and canary duration recommendations.
03:56 Speaker 3 (Leah): good. procurement: we might ask for a 9-12 month term instead of 12 to keep flexibility, is that negotiable?
04:04 Speaker 1 (Maya): we can offer 9-month with prorated pricing — I'll include both 9 and 12 month options.
04:12 Speaker 5 (Omar): if we go with private pilot in EU, what's the earliest start? we need lead time for network peering and certs.
04:20 Speaker 2 (Liam): typical provisioning for private VPC is 2–3 weeks, on-prem more like 6–10 weeks depending on approvals.
04:29 Speaker 3 (Nina): that may push procurement, but we can do hosted-eu as interim.
04:34 Speaker 1 (Maya): yes you can start hosted eu while private pilot is staging.
04:39 Speaker 4 (Carlos): one last thing — any SLA uplift options for tail latency? we need something contractual.
04:46 Speaker 1 (Maya): we have SLA tiers tied to reserved capacity, I'll include the SLA table in the amendment.
04:52 Speaker 3 (Leah): thanks, this is helpful.
04:56 Speaker 1 (Maya): ok to recap: Maya will send amendment + SOC2 + KMS notes + observability pricing by Thurs (2026-08-20). Liam will run perf bench on EU private pilot (mirror prod patterns) and share by Mon (2026-08-24). Carlos will export token usage and peak QPS by Wed (2026-08-19). Leah to confirm procurement decision date by Fri (2026-08-21).
05:20 Speaker 2 (Liam): we'll attach raw bench data and a short README about test assumptions.
05:29 Speaker 3 (Nina): thanks team, schedule the on-prem deep-dive if needed after bench.
05:34 Speaker 1 (Maya): great — we will follow up in email and set the technical deep-dive. thanks everyone, bye.

Action items (inline): Maya: pricing + docs; Liam: perf bench; Carlos: usage data; Leah/Omar: procurement dates.

End of transcript.
